messages:
anya: Quick follow-up from the fused-attn RFC — syncing on kernel selection and the execution-plan interface. TL;DR: we need a clear selector order (fused-QKV -> fused-bias/rope -> dropout-free) + a graceful fallback chain.

mike: +1. My vote is a numeric priority field in the kernel registry. Runtime picks the highest-priority compatible kernel for the current HW/model config.

chun: How do we encode "compatible"? thinking: device_arch, instruction_set, max_seq_len, qkv_layout, requires_dropout flag. Keep it machine-checkable.

sasha: Agree on machine-checkable, but avoid exploding the ModelBackend API. Consider a compact capability bitmask or capability tags instead of many fields.

kevin: Bitmask is compact but opaque. Suggest capability-tags (list of strings) + an integer "score" so operators can tune preference without registry surgery.

theresa: Important: we must keep fallback costs predictable. Kernels should publish a perf_estimate (tokens/ms or ms/token p50/p95) for planning and SLO reasoning.

mike: We can seed perf_estimate from compile-time heuristics and update it with runtime telemetry (autotune). Cache metrics per model-config+hw so decisions stabilize.

anya: Proposed rollout: register new fused kernels behind feature-flag e.g. "attn_fused_v2" -> canary to dedicated QA pool -> validate latency/cost/regression against eval set -> widen.

chun: On the fusion contract: how does fused-bias/rope present itself to the compiler? I propose the fusion stage consumes canonical ModelProto with separate bias+rope fields and emits a kernel_key like "fused_bias_rope_v1".

sasha: Also need partial-fusion semantics: e.g. fused-QKV but rope left unmerged for older models. Runtime selector must allow composable kernels (chainable ops).

kevin: Selector pseudocode idea:
````
candidates = registry.find_compatible(model, hw)
sorted = sort_by((score, perf_estimate))
for k in sorted:
  if k.supports_seq(seq_len):
    return k
return generic_attention
````
(we should also consider memory footprint checks before final selection)

theresa: Telemetry requirements: tag each inference with kernel_name, model_version, seq_len_bucket, dropout_flag, and route info. That makes regression detection and cost comparisons straightforward.

anya: Action items: (1) Draft API for "kernel_capabilities" (chun), (2) Registry schema change to add perf_estimate + score (mike), (3) Canary rollout checklist and monitoring dashboards (sasha), (4) Eval suite comparing dropout-free vs baseline for quality regressions (theresa). Target: EOD next Wed.

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: attn_fused_v2 -> pool:d-qa-3 at 2026-03-25 09:00 UTC :rocket:

anya: thanks all — will collate into a short RFC addendum and link here when done.
